findings.text: follow-on: the added _edit_share docstring ends "the sequence-matcher edit share §22 declares", citing a plan section inside source; the naming rules forbid plan-section references in code and comments, so the file stops standing alone if the plan is renumbered or deleted.

follow-on: _review_coverage_report is called here with no config, and neither this caller nor reckon/crew/recovery.py:494 resolves the flight config, so _plan_review_change_threshold always reads the default 0.30 and a project or host override of review.plan_change_threshold cannot change the production verdict, contradicting the promise at reckon/flight.py:710 that a host or project layer can tighten it without a code change.

follow-on: the evidence list states tests/test_review_is_earned_by_significant_change.py has "(13 cases)", but the file defines 12 test functions and the named 14-passed total is 12 plus the two in tests/test_plan_settle_window_is_declared.py.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 64e6b3376; one product commit (02021245b, plan_review.py/routing.py/flight.py/flight-defaults.yaml/SKILL.md and the two tests) plus three docs commits (c8a1ae305, a5ee88ae4, 0a5e3a893) that add the landing fragment and the replay script; every hunk serves the goal.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names a synthetic-plan series (10% covered, 35% uncovered with the gate refusal naming the section and its measured share; three successive edits covered then uncovered; an added section; a done-when edit; a deferred-to-implementable section; no-snapshot exact-only; a project override; the declared threshold read and validated; one key table; the dispatch tokeniser reused; rule 9; the replay; the interface count; the pytest line N passed EXIT=0); I re-ran the named gate in the reviewed worktree and reproduced 14 passed, EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to cover a plan-review unit whose authored prose changed by less than review.plan_change_threshold against the newest stored review snapshot, with a changed done-when or a newly implementable section uncovered whatever its size; reckon/crew/plan_review.py:598 _review_coverage_report implements the per-unit measure and the three material cases, so the landed change is what the goal states.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, four commits, tests "14 passed, EXIT=0", baseline_suite (base 64e6b3376, 3 failed) and after_suite (head c8a1ae305, 2 failed) with their log paths, and negative-control.log named.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares nine exclusive paths (reckon/crew/plan_review.py, reckon/crew/routing.py, reckon/flight.py, reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml, skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md, tests/test_review_is_earned_by_significant_change.py, tests/test_plan_settle_window_is_declared.py, the landing fragment, and the figures directory); every path in git diff 64e6b3376..0a5e3a893 lies inside them.

justifications.durability: tests/test_review_is_earned_by_significant_change.py drives the real predicate, store and gate over a synthesised mounted project and the cumulative three-edit case fails when the comparator is mutated (logs/negative-control.log, EXIT=1), so the assertions are not merely green.
justifications.evidence: the gate asserts the done-when and its result is recorded (manifest tests "14 passed, EXIT=0" at logs/newtests.log), the base/head suites and their logs are named, and I confirmed public_definitions 1481 at 64e6b3376 against 1482 at head with reckon.interface_counts.
justifications.fit: the additions follow the module's lazy-import and docstring idiom, but the new _edit_share docstring at reckon/crew/plan_review.py:584 cites a plan section, which the repository naming rules forbid in source.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/plan_review.py:598-720 measures each outstanding unit's present prose against the newest covering review's snapshot and leaves a changed done-when, an added section and a newly implementable section uncovered, exactly as the goal states.
justifications.reuse: the measure reuses the owner's tokeniser dispatch._normalised_words and the owner predicates implementable_sections and _section_digests rather than forking a second tokeniser or digest, per reckon/crew/plan_review.py:574-590.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff --stat 64e6b3376..0a5e3a893 lies inside the nine declared write paths, and the two-value _review_coverage is kept beside the new predicate rather than replaced.
